title: Native derived-Weil tensor preserves bounded constructible complexes
statement: Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme. Use the coefficient-ring sheaf $B_X$, abelian Weil-sheaf category $\mathcal W_X$, ambient derived category $D(\mathcal W_X)$ and its bounded constructible full subcategory $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X_0)$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], and the derived tensor $\otimes^L_{B_X}$ with diagonal Weil action of [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations]. For all $A,B\in\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X_0)$ the object $B\otimes^L_{B_X}A$ of $D(\mathcal W_X)$ belongs to $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X_0)$: its cohomology vanishes in all but finitely many degrees, and the underlying $B_X$-module of each of its cohomology sheaves is constructible in the sense of the framework. No internal-Hom or adjunction assertion is part of this statement.

source.place: Step 1, first and fourth Hom bijections: constructibility of the tensor object to which the transposition is applied, in the actual derived-Weil realization (live DerivedHom.lean and the WeilComplex objectProperty). The tensor-Hom adjunction itself is the landed lem-sf-weil-native-closed-forgetful.

proof.text: Let Y be the geometric fiber and aY its structural map to Spec of the algebraic closure of k₀. Base change preserves the separated finite-type hypotheses. The finite-type-over-Noetherian instances give IsNoetherian Y. Algebra.ringChar_eq gives the required characteristic inequality on the algebraic closure.

Apply the first clause of weil_geometric_hom_constructibility to A.obj and B.obj and their subcategory properties. It identifies their native geometric realizations with constant-model bounded constructible objects. Use adicConstructibilityPredicateComparison to identify this predicate with boundedConstructible on Y.

Apply boundedConstructible_tensor_closure for the finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure condensed coefficient to the images of B and A, in that order, on the separated finite-type scheme Y over the algebraic closure. All field and characteristic hypotheses were supplied in step 1.

Take the component at (B.obj,A.obj) of nativeGeometricForget_tensorComparison. Transfer the ordinary tensor result along its inverse, first for boundedness and then through each homology functor for constructibility. Convert back through the same predicate equality and geometric cohomological criterion. This proves precisely the unchanged native tensor membership statement.

proof_origin.place: Step 1, first and fourth tensor transpositions. M1 uses the existing native geometric cohomological criterion and ordinary condensed tensor closure; the remaining coefficient/tensor comparison is split off explicitly.
